rule: `valid` is never, by itself, permission to execute. Authorization APIs expose an explicit decision (`authorized`, or a documented equivalent such as `verified`, `official`, `requested_conditions_met`, `claim_verified`).
method: Enumeration by scripts/check-valid-field-decisions.mjs of every `.valid`, `?.valid`, ["valid"], .get("valid") read and `{ valid } =` destructuring in shipped JS/MJS/CJS/HTML/Python, positive valid-only sinks under test/, and every exit-0 / HTTP-2xx decision sink in JS/Python/Go. Valid-derived aliases (variables, destructuring, helper return values, object properties, imported helpers; Python via its AST) are rewritten to reads before sinks are matched, and their uses are listed. Limits: no flow through arbitrary call arguments, containers, or dynamic property names; see docs/COMMAND_AUTHORIZATION.md.

valid_reads.deny-guard: valid=false denies (throw/return/exit non-zero/skip); a true value only lets later checks run.

valid_reads.schema-check: type or shape check of a verdict field; malformed input is rejected.
valid_reads.consistency-status: selects only a non-authorization outcome: exit 3 (consistent, not authorized) versus failure, a diagnostic field, or a reviewed diagnostic exit.
valid_reads.diagnostic-exit: read inside a reviewed --diagnostic-only branch whose output reports authorized:false and NOT AN AUTHORIZATION DECISION.
valid_reads.assertion: test or self-check assertion; not an execution path.
